verdict.rationale: Svelte's own `$effect` rune runs after the DOM updates and can return teardown functions. That is the lifecycle hook a developer would use to initialise and clean up a third-party library on rendered elements. The evidence never shows getting a direct element reference or integrating a charting or visualization library, so support is only implied. Missing for 10: documented element references (e.g. bind:this), actions/attachments for DOM integration, any example of integrating a charting or visualization library, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can directly manipulate the DOM to integrate existing browser libraries like charting or visualization tools

citations.quote: Effects run after the DOM updates and can return teardown functions.
$effect executes functions when reactive state changes.
